text:
jess: Heads up, brought up iris-embed-v1 (1024d) on the onboarding harness. Did float32 -> int4 (symmetric) quant with default calibrator. Seeing R@1 drop ~0.05 on the search holdout.
jess: float32 R@1=0.845, int4=0.796, R@50 unchanged.
ojmar: typo — you mean omar?
omar: lol yes. which quant path? hf->onnx->tvm?
jess: hf->onnx->quantize (our torchscript path) -> runtime. Same preprocessing. mean pooling.
fran: int4 is aggressive, especially for 1024 dims. how's cosine shift distribution?
jess: mean cos shift per-sample = -0.022, std=0.007. centroid norms shrink ~6%. top topical cohorts see nearest-neighbor swaps.
ryan: can you run int8 and int4-perchannel asymmetric? int4 per-channel often helps if supported. Also try PCA reduction to 512 pre-quant to test sensitivity.
jess: started an int8 run now. also queued PCA-512 then quant int4 (just as an experiment).
eval-bot: Job 1767778888-iris-eval queued. artifacts will land at https://redwood.internal/artifacts/1767778888
omar: also check whether tokenization differences changed drop-in normalization (we had a tokenizer edge where trailing spaces changed embedding norms).
fran: let's get a kNN flip matrix (float32 vs int4) and a per-cohort R@1,R@5 table. small script: `python knn_flip.py --base float32 --variant int4 --k 5 --out flips.csv`
jess: done, uploaded flips.csv and flip-summary.png to artifacts. notable flips: product-related queries swapped from correct to brand-near neighbours.
ryan: that pattern smells like direction preservation but scale compression. try post-quant rescale using global centroid norm ratio as a diagnostic: `emb_q *= (mean_norm_fp32/mean_norm_q)` and re-eval.
jess: will try rescale. also trying calibration set A vs B (A=wiki+web, B=search-headlines) to see if calibrator sampling changes quant scales.
eval-bot: Job 1767778888-iris-eval completed 10 artifacts uploaded (embeddings.csv, flips.csv, recall_k.csv, cohort_stats.json).
omar: initial int8 result: R@1=0.839 (good), int4-perchannel-asym: R@1=0.833 (better than symmetric). plain int4 symmetric worst.
fran: PCA-512 before int4 gave R@1=0.825 - intermediate. post-quant rescale recovered ~0.018 of the gap.
ryan: sounds like action items: 1) prefer int8 for iris in recommendations, 2) if int4 needed, use per-channel asymmetric with careful calibration + consider PCA compression as a controlled trade-off, 3) add rescale diagnostic to our eval harness.
jess: I'll draft a short note for the quant-recommendations doc and link these artifacts. will also open a ticket to add per-cohort flip diffs in the weekly bakeoff.
omar: agree. if we still need a smaller mem footprint, consider hybrid approach: split dims (0:512 int8, 512:1024 int4) and measure.
fran: please don't forget to run a small prod canary (0.1% traffic) for int4-perchannel before any rollout.
jess: ack, creating canary plan. assigning to omar for canary run.
eval-bot: Canary plan template: https://redwood.internal/templates/canary-plan.md
omar: will run canary after bench passes. pinged infra for capacity.
ryan: thanks all. summary: int4 symmetric not recommended; per-channel asymmetric + calibration tweaks may be acceptable with canary. hold rollout until canary passes. :thumbsup:
